correctness.rationale: For each marked set K of serial positions, all later choosers avoid the assigned schools of the marked predecessors with independent conditional probability (n-t+1)/(n-t+1+a_t); the coupon process gives the identical probability that marked first-appearance types never recur. The product telescopes to r!/prod_s(n-k_s+s); inclusion-exclusion identifies the entire Bernoulli indicator joint law. DA coupon representation is reconstructed using iid proposal streams, square-market termination when each school first receives a proposal, and one-proposer school iff its assigned student is unenvied. Direct covariance, variance and moment asymptotics follow. Executed stdlib exact verification for all 331997 RSD profiles n<=4, 46673 DA profiles n<=3 and all subset identities through n=8; experiments are supporting evidence, not the proof for arbitrary n.

value.rationale: Genuine distributional bridge between two widely used matching mechanisms, stronger than the known coinciding H_n means. The explicit all-subsets probability product identifies the exact positive pairwise dependence and fluctuations under RSD, and transports the coupon limit to both algorithms. It makes concrete an intuitively unobvious equivalence about equity of assignments in finite random school-choice markets, with clear scope and no claim of pointwise coupling.
